FY2025/26 field work: fertiliser programme completed (123% with carry-over stock), circle spraying 78% (2.35 of 3 rounds), selective 92%, pruning 74%; glyphosate over-spraying and a 3-month dry spell left about 10% bare ground (PA, Aug 2026).

issues.title: Mixed exchange rates hide a 24% cost overrun
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 converts actuals at IDR4,414 per RM but the budgets for upkeep, harvesting and dispatch at IDR3,412 (Table 15 headers '4414-IDR' vs '3412-IDR'; Tables 8 and 19 reproduce it), while the general-charges budget uses 4,414. Table 18 (IDR): ex-estate IDR1,496,924/t vs IDR1,211,338 budget (+24%); upkeep IDR844,769 vs 652,133 (+30%); harvesting & collection IDR363,526 vs 281,387 (+29%). Table 19 (RM) and 9.1 report RM339.11 vs RM335.78, '1% above'; upkeep RM3,865.92/ha vs RM3,861.10 (Table 8) although IDR17,065,619 vs 13,174,075/ha is +30%. Only 7.9 mentions the IDR overrun. At one rate the RM budget would be about RM274/t (IDR1,211,338 / 4,414, calc).

actions.item: Replace dead supply palms and supply vacant points (about 8,000 seedlings), starting when Arwana nursery seedlings are ready; replace flood-killed 2025 planting immediately
Improve cambered bunds in the immature area so floods do not kill young palms
Re-census palms after supplying; verify the abnormal SPH drop in P18–P20
Verify planted size of each field
Train sprayers and staff to stop glyphosate over-spraying; glyphosate in palm circles only, stop blanket Paraquat + Ally once soft grasses dominate (2.0 m circles)
Resume establishing soft grasses and Nephrolepis in inter-rows
Keep spraying Stenochlaena, sedges and noxious broadleaf every 3 months (Paraquat + Ally or Triclopyr), esp. Div 3 and 4 and newly planted areas
Finish removing jungle trees; poison with Garlon + diesel
Raise sprayer output from 3.5 to 5.0 ha/man-day
Raise manuring output from 20 toward 25 bags/man-day (wheelbarrows, longer hours)
Use the 15 composting workers for manuring when needed
Mechanise compost application to raise output
Keep harvesting intervals at 10–15 days (now 6–11) to raise harvester output; enforce loose fruit collection; fill any harvester shortage before peak
Raise harvester productivity (1.37–1.98 t/man-day, low in 2019–2020 plantings)
Start a mechanised infield FFB collection pilot (Startrac, 5 harvesters per machine)
Run the mechanised collection pilot properly: 4 skilled cutters + 2 helpers per machine, target 2.5–3.0 t/man-day and 20–24 t/machine-day, share income evenly, record output and vehicle costs
Consider paying harvesters every three months
Reduce internal transport; move FFB direct from platform to mill as lateriting progresses
Laterite the raised and compacted collection roads first; raise, compact and sun-harden the rest in the rehabilitation area, then laterite next FY
Service vehicles on schedule; sell or write off badly damaged vehicles; check Startrac and backhoe running costs (30–189% over budget)
Postpone the main water gate installation
Manage water better in heavy rain and drought (keep drains at 50–75 cm)
Resume Oryctes and leaf-eating caterpillar treatment in immature fields; stay alert for caterpillars in dry weather
Start harvesting the 2020 immature field
Anti-theft: boundary trenches, regular patrols, no FFB left overnight on boundaries, stagger harvest days vs village plots
Resume rehabilitating the 339.84 ha plantable vacant land once road access is ready
Bring FY2025/26 manuring up to date after first-half deviation
Use carried-over NK Mixture as 1:1 substitute for Mix B
Submit complete manuring records; clarify HGFB and ZA stock left after 'completed' programmes
Apply fertiliser in weeded circles (not frond heaps) within two months of receipt; suspend in flooded areas
Resume manuring in previously neglected areas without delay
No cut in Inti inorganic fertiliser; compost priority to Plasma

Correct under-pruning (HG35, HL24, HL39, HK24) and over-pruning in young palms; stack fronds among four palms
Prepare P23 for crop recovery in second half of FY2026/27; prune only senescent fronds
Lower high water tables to 45–60 cm (desilt, clear blockages, maintain gates, weirs, outlets, culverts)
Quarterly rat census in every field; bait only at 10% damage
Monitor parthenocarpy; reassess leaf nutrients this year
Merge small sub-blocks (esp. P17, P22) toward 40–60 ha and install clear block labels
Re-check reported estate average yield (FY2024/25 21.25 t/ha; PA 2/2026 gives 18.37)

HARUAN ESTATE (INTI), PT Lifere Agro Kapuas (PT LAK), Kalimantan, UMB group. Fact pack from PA Report 2/2026 (Planting Advisor En Adnan Bin Mustafa, visit 18 and 20 August 2026, review period May 2025 to April 2026, full 12 months of FY2025/26; previous PA visit 5-6 Feb 2026) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Agronomist Mr Chong Kuan Ming, visit 19 May 2026; previous visit 26 Nov 2025). Plantation Director Mr Tee Tong Heng; Senior Manager Bpk Deni Irawan; Estate Manager Bpk Lalu Suryandi (Agro cover still names former manager Bpk Richard Frenky Sibuea). Financial year May to April. PA money is in IDR with RM conversions: actuals at IDR4,414 per RM, but budgets for upkeep, harvesting and dispatch at IDR3,412 (general charges budget at 4,414), so RM budget comparisons understate overruns. Figures are Inti only unless stated; labour covers Inti and Plasma.

HEADLINE FY2025/26 (May 2025-Apr 2026, PA): FFB 29,699.86 t, 20.20 t/ha vs budget 29,791.65 t, 20.26 t/ha (in line); FY2024/25 27,057.87 t, 18.37 t/ha (+10%). Ex-estate cost RM339.11/t vs RM335.78 (+1%); in IDR 1,496,924 vs 1,211,338/t (+24%). PA verdict: performance acceptable.

AREA (PA Table 1, Apr 2026): title 2,300.38 ha; planted 1,599.96 (mature 1,470.18, immature 129.78); building sites and roads 147.01; vacant plantable 339.84; vacant unplantable 213.57. No change to Apr 2026. By Jul 2026 mature 1,522.47 ha and immature 77.49 ha after 52.29 ha (2020 planting) declared mature in May 2026 (PA 11.5 still quotes 51.87 ha). Rehabilitation of plantable vacant land started with an access road; resume once road access is ready. By planting (Agro Table 1): 2012 357.42 ha, 2013 713.14, 2015 72.42, 2016 121.07, 2017 7.66, 2018 70.49, 2019 116.86, 2020 11.12 mature + 51.87 immature, 2022 0.42, 2023 31.92, 2024 30.60, 2025 14.97. PA Table 2 by division (mature): Div 1 236.74 ha (136 SPH), Div 2 59.37 (143), Div 3 606.24 (139), Div 4 567.83 (124); mature 195,487 palms, 133 SPH; immature 16,490 palms, 127 SPH; estate 211,977 palms, 132 SPH. Agro: 134 sub-blocks averaging 11.9 ha; merge small blocks (esp. P17, P22) to 40-60 ha; block labels inadequate. No replanting needed for five years.

PALM DENSITY (Agro Table 3, SPH 2021 vs current): 2012 149 to 145; 2013 139 to 136; 2015 138; 2016 132; 2017 125 to 128; 2018 148 to 102 (-31.1%); 2019 135 to 95 (-29.6%); 2020 143 to 106 (-25.9%); 2022 102; 2023 143; 2024 140; 2025 143; total 141 to 132 (-6.4%). The P18-P20 drop is abnormal and must be verified. Very low stands (PA Table 2, Apr 2026): HK37-19C1 13 SPH, HF38-19A1 27, HD40-19A1 29, HK38-20A1 40, HD36-19A1 52, HG38-20A1 52, HD38-18A1 55, HK38-16B1 61. Supply (Agro Table 4): plan FY25-26 82.12 ha / 11,743 palms; actually planted May 2025-Apr 2026 41.84 ha / 5,986 palms. About 8,000 more seedlings needed; many supplied palms died from flooding. PA Aug 2026: supplying starts once seedlings in Arwana nursery are ready; the 2025 planting (F36-25B1, F37-25A1) died from flooding and must be replaced now; improve cambered bunds.

STAFF AND LABOUR (PA Tables 3-4): manager, KTU (Muhammad Rusli) and 4 assistants, unchanged. Checkroll (Inti and Plasma, 2,559.05 ha): Apr 2026 311 vs 355 required (1 per 8 ha); Jul 2026 301 (1 per 9 ha), sufficient. Harvester/carrier 143 in Apr vs 140 required, 137 in Jul (1 per 18 ha over 2,422.76 ha mature). Apr 2026: FFB lorry 16 vs 29, manuring 27 vs 30 (12 in Jul), spraying 38 vs 39 (30 in Jul), pruner 8 vs 12, general worker 17 vs 30, tractor driver 7 vs 19. 15 composting workers in Jul can help manuring.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Tables 5-6, Appendix 1, 12 months, 2,494.08 ha basis): excluding depreciation and amortisation RM1,941,894 (IDR8,572,242,745) = RM779 (IDR3,437,031)/ha vs RM745 (IDR3,289,235), 5% over, acceptable. Over budget: staff bonus +180%, staff accommodation +21%, labour BPJS Kesehatan +37%, labour recruitment +12% (137 workers vs 75 budgeted), general office (text 12%, appendix 28%), telecommunication +96% (Starlink), ISPO +216% (PPE, signboard), office and compound repairs +150%.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Tables 7-8, 12 months, 1,470.18 ha): total RM5,683,604 = RM3,865.92/ha vs RM3,861.10 budget (in IDR 17,065,619 vs 13,174,075/ha, +30%). RM/ha actual vs budget: supervision 12.97 vs 40.24; selective spraying and lallang 155.87 vs 191.71; manuring total 1,893.20 vs 2,326.81 (material 1,749.00 vs 2,216.27; labour 64.97; contract 53.83 unbudgeted; transport 25.39); composting 350.15 vs 347.91; P&D 2.11 vs 18.04; census 3.99; drains 87.73 vs 72.07; roads and bridges 1,168.03 vs 526.26 (122% over: laterite from Banjarmasin RM89,901, machine rental RM106,380); soil and water 17.70 vs 25.30; supplying 80.94 vs 150.11; pruning 86.93 vs 138.29; tools 4.53; other 1.77.

WEEDING (PA 6.1, FY2025/26): circle and path (Table 9) 3,460.13 of 4,410.54 ha, 2.35 of 3 rounds, 78% (Div 1 84%, Div 2 82%, Div 3 80%, Div 4 74%); only 1 round in HK39-16B1, HJ43-12A1, HJ44-12A1, HJ39-13A1, HJ40-13A1, HJ41-13A1, HJ42-13A1, HH39-13A1, HG38-15A1, HG39-15C1, HG37-19A1. Circles clean from blanket Paraquat + Ally 20DF, to stop once soft grasses dominate; glyphosate over-spraying and the dry spell caused bare ground; train sprayers. 3.50 ha/man-day (target 5.0) at IDR55,000 (RM12.46)/ha, pay IDR192,500 (RM43.61)/day. Selective (Table 10): 3,931.46 ha of printed 4,253.49 ha, 2.7 rounds, 92% (block rows add to 4,410.54 ha, 89%). Inter-row: bare ground about 10%; soft grass about 40% (spray Ally and/or Triclopyr by mist blower); soft grass with noxious and resilient weeds about 20% along drains and low ground; Stenochlaena, sedges and broadleaf dominance about 30% in rehabilitated areas, Div 3 and 4 (Paraquat + Ally or Triclopyr every 3 months, CKS power sprayer). Aggressive Stenochlaena spraying in Div 3-4 satisfactory. Resume establishing soft grasses and Nephrolepis.
WEEDING (Agro 4.5, FY2025/26): two interrow and circle rounds done in all prime plantings, third partial (P17 interrow complete); bare ground in P12, P15, P16 from over-spraying; Asystasia, woodies, VOP, wild brinjal in P13; Stenochlaena reduced; P17 circles overgrown; young mature vegetation markedly improved.

MANURING (PA Table 11, FY2025/26): programme completed; overall lines 2,667,585 kg applied of 2,169,760 kg programme (printed totals 5,335,170 of 4,339,520, 123%, double-count and are kg not tonnes). Mix B 1,575,875 of 1,564,300 (101%); ZA 101%; RP 100%; MOP 133%; compound 14.13.9.2.5 78%; urea 99%; kieserite 99%; HGFB 212%; carry-over NPK mixture 424,450, NPK 12 12 17 2 22,910, NPK 15.15.6.4 10,600, compound 13:6:27 22,400, Kaptan 400. Excess from agronomist's additional fertiliser and last FY carry-over. No manuring at visit (dry spell); broadcasting by wheelbarrow; 20 bags/man-day at RM1.81 (IDR8,000)/bag, target 25.
MANURING (Agro section 3, FY2025/26): programme 3,315.11 mt, applied 3,968.15 mt (120%): Mix B 2,496.23 of 2,504.15; NK 10.5/30 595.40 (carry-over, used 1:1 for Mix B); ZA 211.50 (101%); RP 542.75; HGFB 1.40 (212%); MOP 25.91 (134%); kieserite 9.70; compound 18.15 of 24.25 (75%); urea 6.45. Delays not assessable (no data). HGFB and ZA stock remain though reported complete. Apply within two months of receipt; suspend in flooded areas; apply in weeded circles, not frond heaps. Note PA and Agro tonnages differ for Mix B, RP and NK.
COMPOST: PA RM350.15/ha vs 347.91, 140 kg per two palms (about 10 t/ha) on frond stacks by wheelbarrow, 40 points/man-day, mechanise. Agro: 10,753 mt allocated over 537.7 ha at 20 t/ha; coverage incomplete and uneven (7% to 388% of area), roadside dumping; analysis within spec; no cut in Inti inorganic fertiliser; prioritise Plasma and non-flooded areas.

PESTS: PA - no significant bagworm or caterpillar outbreak; rat baiting done in immature and young areas, minimal rat attack controlled; RM2.11/ha (15% of budget in IDR). Agro - rat census Nov 2025-Jan 2026 L1 5.76%, L2 4.56% (highest HL29-12A2 11.79%); no baiting needed, census every field quarterly, bait at 10%. No bagworm; Ganoderma negligible.

PRUNING: PA Table 12 FY2025/26 2,185.47 of 2,940.36 ha (74%; Div 1 66%, Div 2 100%, Div 3 84%, Div 4 65%), by payments; RM0.80 (IDR3,300)/palm/year; appearance satisfactory; fronds now stacked in heaps among four palms. Agro Table 10: YP2012 85%, 2013 82%, 2015 82%, 2016 62%, 2017 88%; under-pruning in HG35, HL24, HL39, HK24; over-pruning in short and young palms; fronds left in circles in HK48.

HARVESTING (PA section 7): manual cutter-and-carrier with mistblower. Harvester output by planting (Table 13, rate IDR/t, t/man-day, earnings): 2012 103,000, 1.59, RM37.14; 2013 108,000, 1.43, RM34.98; 2015 123,000, 1.58, RM44.00; 2016 123,000, 1.37, RM38.08; 2017 108,000, 1.98, RM48.49; 2018 145,000, 1.60, RM52.56; 2019 145,000, 1.56, RM51.17; 2020 123,000, 1.89, RM52.69; minimum wage RM31.54. Apr 2026 (Table 14): intervals 6-11 days (mostly 8), 2-3 rounds per month, 33-41 rounds per FY; PA wants 10-15 days. Cost (Table 15, RM/t, actual vs budget at 3,412): supervision 3.23 vs 3.43; harvesting 34.95 vs 37.84; infield loading 9.12 vs 6.93; internal transport 17.50 vs 14.68; tools 0.85; external transport 16.71 vs 18.56; total RM82.36 vs 82.48, but IDR363,526 vs 281,387 (+30%). Mechanised infield collection pilot in HL48-16B1 (rubber-track vehicle, 6 harvesters, driver, loader); target 2.5-3.0 t/man-day, 20-24 t/machine-day; share income evenly; record costs.
HARVESTING (Agro 4.1, Table 9): monthly intervals May 2025-Apr 2026 by division 6-13 days; at the May 2026 visit slightly over 15 days (festivals). Bunch checks: P13-HF35 8% over-ripe and 2% rotten, P15-HG38 8% over-ripe, others under 2%. Loose fruit in HF35, oxidised in HK24. P12 rounds to Apr 2026 101% of 36 target. Rotten bunches in P19 and P20; over-ripe and empty bunches at HK49 platforms.

CROP (PA Table 17, FY2025/26 12 months, 1,470.18 ha): FFB 29,699.86 t vs 29,791.65 budget; 20.20 vs 20.26 t/ha; last year 27,057.87 t, 18.37 t/ha on 1,472.79 ha. CPO 6,094.41 t (budget 6,405.20), OER 20.52% vs 21.50% (last year 19.47%); kernel 1,009.80 t, KER 3.40% vs 4.00% (2.93%); CPO 4.15 t/ha vs 4.36 (3.58).
YIELD (Agro Table 14, FY2024/25 vs FY2025/26): P12 26.87 to 24.21 (-9.9%); P13 18.48 to 20.08 (+8.7%); P15 14.69 to 25.75 (+75.3%); P16 12.64 to 16.63 (+31.6%); P17 23.74 to 30.22 (+27.3%); P18 9.23 to 12.14 (+31.5%); P19 6.65 to 13.36 (+100.9%); P20 2.96 to 18.33 (+519%); estate printed 21.25 to 20.20 (-4.9%), but the agronomist asks to verify; the block rows give 18.38 for FY2024/25 and the PA prints 18.37, so the estate actually rose about 10%. Drivers: crop recovery, nutrition, young palms maturing. P13, P16 below potential; P18, P19 below expectations. Limiting factors: low stand, longer intervals and loose fruit, delayed manuring, over-pruning in young mature, residual weeds.

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA Tables 18-19, FY2025/26, RM/t FFB actual vs budget): general charges 65.38 vs 62.77; upkeep and cultivation 191.37 vs 190.54; harvesting and collection 65.65 vs 63.91; dispatch and storage 16.71 vs 18.56; ex-estate 339.11 vs 335.78 (IDR1,496,924 vs 1,211,338, +24%); processing 10.27 vs 12.41; head/regional office 7.26 vs 7.53; depreciation/amortisation 84 vs 130; grand total RM441 vs 487/t FFB. Unlike PA 1/2026, dispatch now has an actual, so no like-for-like adjustment is needed. PA: cost acceptable.

ROADS, DRAINS, SECURITY (PA 6.6-6.9): main road fully laterited; laterite collection roads next; remaining rehab-area roads to be raised, compacted and sun-hardened 3-6 months then laterited next FY. Estate dry for over 3 months before the Aug visit; collection drains mostly dry; water team traps river water; keep water 50-75 cm below ground; drains RM87.73/ha vs 72.07. FFB theft risk high from settlers' plots inside the estate: boundary trenches, patrols, no FFB left overnight at boundaries.
VEHICLES (PA Table 20): Startrac mini tractors 30-125% over budget, backhoe +189%, one Yanmar +56%; service on schedule, sell or write off damaged units.

AGRONOMY FIELD NOTES (Agro sections 4-6): low-lying P12, P13, P16 stunted with orange spotting (K deficiency); unattended palms in HL39, HF39, HK48; foliar N and K improved (Oct 2025 leaf: estate N 2.75, P 0.150, K 1.21, Mg 0.31, B 18.89); resample this year for FY2027/28. Parthenocarpy now insignificant. Acid sulfate soils: keep water table 45-60 cm; high water in HJ45, HJ46, HK45. Immature: P23 and P24 supplied Jul-Sep 2025 with overgrown seedlings, vigour improved, chlorosis in HF36 and HF40, poor bunch development; P23 crop from second half FY2026/27; prune only senescent fronds. Supply palms: CRF 600 g + RP 500 g in the hole.

FERTILISER PROGRAMME FY2026/27 (Agro Appendix 1, unchanged; grams per palm): P2012 Mix B 2,500 Jun and Sep, RP 1,700 Oct, Mix B 2,200 Dec and Mar. P2013/P2015 Mix B 2,200 Jun and Sep, RP 1,700 Oct, Mix B 2,000 Dec and Mar. P2016 Mix B 2,200 May and Aug, RP 1,700 Oct, Mix B 2,000 Nov and Feb. P2017 Mix B 2,500 May and Aug, RP 2,000 Oct, Mix B 2,200 Nov and Feb. P2018/P2019 Mix B 2,200 May and Aug, RP 2,000 Oct, Mix B 2,000 Nov and Feb. P2020 Mix B 1,700 May and Aug, RP 2,000 Sep, Mix B 2,000 Nov and Feb. P2022/2023 Mix B 1,500 May and Aug, RP 2,000 Sep, Mix B 1,500 Nov and Feb. P2024 compound 1,000 May, 1,200 Aug, RP 1,700 Sep, compound 1,200 Nov, 1,500 Feb. P2025 compound 800 May, 900 Aug, RP 1,500 Sep, compound 1,000 Nov, 1,200 Feb. Mix B = 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate.
